meta.title: Five Questions for Nurse Jill
meta.textType: functional: an interview with five questions, for the class blog

paragraphs: Posted by May. On Wednesday, February tenth, after lunch, I went to the nurse's room with my notebook and a pencil. I sat at the desk, and Nurse Jill sat next to me with a smile. A poster on the wall said "WASH YOUR HANDS," and a glass cabinet stood behind us. I had five questions for the blog, and Teacher Kim read this post first. "Please ask your first question," said Nurse Jill.

These are my five questions. Question one: "What does a school nurse do?" Question two: "Which problems are the most common?" Question three: "How much sleep do children need?" Question four: "What should children eat and drink?" Question five: "Do you like your job?" For question one, Nurse Jill said, "I see about fifteen children every day." She helps children who feel ill or have a small accident. She listens to each child, and she checks the temperature. For question two, she said, "Headaches and tired children are the most common problems." Tired children usually come to her after lunch.

Nurse Jill pointed at another poster near the door. It said "SLEEP, WATER, FRUIT, EXERCISE." It had four drawings: a moon, a glass of water, an apple, and a running shoe. "Children need at least nine hours of sleep," she said. "The brain needs a rest, so go to bed early." "Eating fresh fruit every day is helpful." "Fast food and sweet drinks give energy for only a short time." "Drinking water is better." "Daily exercise is important, because it helps children relax." "Walking to school is good exercise, too," she said.

Nurse Jill also told readers to wash their hands before they eat. She told them to brush their teeth in the morning and at night. "A child must tell a teacher at once when a friend feels ill," she said. "A friend may be too shy to ask for help," she added. I wrote every answer in my notebook. I asked my last question: "Do you like your job?" "Yes, because I help children feel better," said Nurse Jill.

"The answers are clear," said Teacher Kim. Then Lily put my post on the blog. I think that these tips are easy. Which tip will you follow? Please tell us in the comments. I will go to bed early tonight.
text.summary: May asks Nurse Jill five questions for the class blog. Nurse Jill talks about the children she sees, sleep, food and water, and her job, and May posts the answers.
